mainTopic: When a witness who falsely denies knowing testimony is liable for a false שבועת העדות: דבר הגורם לממון, cases everyone agrees on, תוך כדי דיבור, and two sets of witnesses.
overview: This amud looks at when a witness who falsely swears he knows nothing is liable for a שבועת העדות. It first explains that the dispute about witnesses of a סוטה concerns עדי סתירה. The question there is whether something that leads to a money loss counts as money. The גמרא then gives cases where everyone agrees the witness is liable. One case is where both sides are suspect about oaths, so the borrower cannot swear and must pay. Another is רבי אבא's case of a man who grabbed a silver bar: he must swear but cannot, so he pays. רב פפא adds that a witness to a husband's death is exempt if he already told the wife, since she is believed on her own word. He is liable if he told no one. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and explains that its case of one denying and one admitting is about a quick retraction. That teaches the rule of תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי, and the גמרא shows why רבי יוחנן still needs both clauses. Finally, it asks why the first of two sets of witnesses is liable, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute about סוטה witnesses is about witnesses of seclusion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the argument about witnesses of a סוטה is about עדי סתירה. It then gives the reason for each side: does something that leads to a money loss count as money?
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument about סוטה witnesses is about witnesses who saw her go into seclusion. One opinion holds that something which causes a money result counts as money, so the witness is liable. The other opinion holds that it does not count as money, so he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining which witnesses of a סוטה the earlier dispute is talking about. It also gives the reason behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony about seclusion is not directly about money. However, it can lead to the woman losing her כתובה. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that such an indirect money result counts as money, so a שבועת העדות applies. חכמים hold that it does not count, so the witness is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses in the case of a wife suspected of being unfaithful
Witnesses who saw the wife go into seclusion with the man her husband warned her about
Something that leads to a money result, without being money itself

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of דבר הגורם לממון is the key tool for the rest of the sugya. Each later case asks how directly the witness's testimony would have caused a money loss.

phrases.english: And the dispute regarding witnesses of a סוטה —
is about witnesses of seclusion;
phrases.notes: These witnesses saw her go into seclusion after her husband had warned her.

phrases.english: One master holds: something that causes a money result
is like money — and he is liable,
and the other master holds: it is not like money —
and he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dispute from the earlier text, which comes before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of עדי סתירה, liability for שבועת העדות depends on whether דבר הגורם לממון counts as money.

steps.title: Two cases where everyone agrees the witness is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists two cases that everyone agrees on. The first is when the other side is suspected about oaths. The second is the single-witness case of רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees about a case where the other party is suspected about oaths. Everyone also agrees about one witness, as in the case of רבי אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists two cases where even those who usually exempt the witness agree that he is liable. This sets up the next steps, which explain the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases, one witness's testimony would have led to a money result so directly that everyone treats it as a money case. The next steps work out exactly when that is true.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposing party, the other side in the case
Suspected of swearing falsely, so not allowed to take an oath

phrases.english: All agree where his opposing party
is suspect regarding oaths,
all agree regarding one witness
of רבי אבא's case.
phrases.notes: The גמרא tells this story a little later, in step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּשֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the dispute, it lists the cases that no one disputes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the 'suspect counterpart' case and in רבי אבא's single-witness case, everyone agrees the witness is liable.

steps.title: Who is the suspect person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first case again and asks which party is the one suspected about oaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All agree where his opposing party is suspect about oaths.' Who is the one who is suspect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first agreed case so it can explain it. It asks who exactly is suspected about oaths, which prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case only works if the witness's testimony would have directly caused payment. That depends on who is suspect, so the גמרא has to identify him.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the one who is suspect?

phrases.english: All agree where his opposing party
is suspect regarding oaths —
who is the suspect one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the first case from step 2 in order to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which party, the borrower, the lender, or both, is the one suspected about oaths?

steps.title: First try: the borrower is suspect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the borrower is the suspect one. The lender then tells the witness: if you had testified, I would have sworn and collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the borrower is suspect, the lender says to the witness: 'If you had come and testified for me, I would have sworn and taken my money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer: the suspect one is the borrower who denies the loan. This answer is tentative and gets tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one witness makes the borrower swear. If the borrower is suspect, he cannot swear, so the lender swears instead and collects. So the lender claims that the witness's silence cost him his money.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)
I would swear and take the money

phrases.english: If you say the borrower is suspect,
where the lender says to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the witness who falsely swore he knew nothing.

phrases.english: If you had come and testified for me,
I would have sworn and taken the money;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first possible answer to the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentatively, the suspect is the borrower, so the lender would have sworn and collected.

steps.title: Rejected: who says you would have sworn?
steps.stepSummary: The witness can answer that there is no proof the lender would really have sworn. So the money loss is too indirect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the witness can say to him: 'Who says you would have sworn?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first try. The witness can say it is not certain the lender would have taken the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the lender only collects if he chooses to swear. That makes the witness only a distant cause of the loss. Since that is too uncertain for everyone to agree he is liable, the suggestion fails.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him
Who says? There is no certainty

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The witness is answering the lender.

phrases.english: Who says that you would have sworn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the case is about a suspect borrower alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The loss would depend on the lender's own choice to swear, so the witness's link to the loss is uncertain and indirect.
steps.confusionAlert: The borrower really is suspect in this case. The problem is not that. The problem is that payment would still depend on the lender actually swearing, so the witness did not directly cause it.

steps.title: The answer: both sides are suspect
steps.stepSummary: The case is where both borrower and lender are suspect. Then the oath goes back to the borrower, who cannot swear, so he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where both of them are suspect. As the master said: the oath goes back to the one who was obligated to take it, and since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the case is where both parties are suspected about oaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both are suspect, the oath goes back to the borrower, who was the one obligated to take it. He cannot swear, so he must pay automatically. Now the single witness's testimony would have directly caused payment, with no 'who says you'd swear?' problem, so everyone agrees he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: That both of them are suspect
The oath goes back to the one obligated to take it
Since he cannot swear, he pays

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees the witness is liable only when his testimony would have led to payment automatically. When both sides are suspect, the borrower cannot swear and must pay, so the witness would have directly caused that payment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the line between a direct money result, where everyone agrees, and an uncertain one that depends on someone's choice, which is not enough.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where both of them are suspect,
as the master said:
the oath returns to the one obligated in it,
phrases.notes: Here that is the borrower, who was first supposed to swear.

phrases.english: and since he cannot swear —
he pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting step 4, it gives the correct case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both parties are suspect, so the oath goes back to the borrower, who cannot swear and must pay. The witness's testimony would directly cause that payment.

steps.title: The story behind רבי אבא's single-witness case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second agreed case again and tells the story behind it: a man grabbed a silver bar, one witness saw it, and the grabber said, 'Yes, I took it, but it was mine.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees in the case of the single witness of רבי אבא. A man grabbed a silver bar from another man. The owner came before רבי אמי while רבי אבא was sitting there. He brought one witness who said the man really did grab it. The grabber said: 'Yes, I grabbed it, but I grabbed what is mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second case from Step 2 and explains it by telling the story. This sets up the legal problem that רבי אמי raises next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is only one witness, and normally one witness cannot force someone to pay. But the grabber himself admits that he took the bar. He only claims it belonged to him, and that admission is what makes the case hard.

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד אֶחָד דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא –
phrases.english: All agree in the case of the one witness of Rabbi Abba —
phrases.notes: This is the second case from the list in Step 2. Now the גמרא explains what happened there.

phrases.english: for there was a certain man who grabbed a silver bar from his fellow.
He came before Rabbi Ami,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the owner, the one whose bar was taken.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Abba was sitting before him;
he went and brought one witness
that he really did grab it from him.
He said to him: 'Yes, I grabbed it —'
'but I grabbed what is mine.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד אֶחָד דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first agreed case was settled in Step 6. Now the גמרא turns to the second agreed case from Step 2 and gives its background story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: one witness says the man grabbed the bar, and the grabber admits it but claims the bar was his.

steps.title: רבי אמי asks how to judge this case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי lists three possible rulings and rejects each one. He cannot make the grabber pay, he cannot let him go, and he cannot let him swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: How should judges rule here? Should he pay? There are not two witnesses! Should he be let off? But there is one witness who says he grabbed it! Should he swear? Since he said 'Yes, I grabbed it, but it was mine,' he is like a robber!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי is stuck, and he shows why each possible ruling seems wrong. This sets up רבי אבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying needs two witnesses. Being let off ignores the one witness, and one witness normally brings an oath. But an oath is not possible either, because by admitting he grabbed the bar, the man has the status of a גזלן, and a גזלן is not trusted to swear.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber, who is not trusted to take an oath

steps.confusionAlert: The grabber is not proven to be a thief. He is treated 'like' a גזלן only because he admits he grabbed the bar, and grabbing, even something you say is yours, puts him in that category for oaths.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
How should judges judge this case?
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. Either way, the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: Let him pay? There are not two witnesses!
Let them exempt him?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִיכָּא חַד סָהֲדָא דְּמִחְטָף חֲטַף!
phrases.english: But there is one witness that he grabbed it!
Let him swear?
Since he said, 'Yes, I grabbed it, but I grabbed what is mine,'
he is like a robber!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the legal problem that comes out of the story in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ruling fits a case with one witness, where the defendant cannot swear because he admits that he grabbed the item?

steps.title: רבי אבא: He must swear but cannot, so he pays
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that the grabber is obligated to swear because of the one witness. Since he cannot swear, he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: He is someone who is obligated to swear and cannot swear. Anyone who is obligated to swear and cannot swear must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא solves רבי אמי's problem with a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one witness creates an obligation to swear. The grabber's status as a גזלן blocks him from swearing, and that turns the oath obligation into an obligation to pay. So here a single witness directly causes a money payment, which explains why everyone agrees about this case in Step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: מחויב שבועה ואינו יכול לישבע משלם: if you must swear but cannot, you pay. In רבי אבא's case this rule means one witness can make someone pay, so all agree about that witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that a single witness can sometimes cause a real money loss. That is the reason this case fits the list of cases 'everyone agrees' on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ מְחוּיָּב שְׁבוּעָה וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִישָּׁבַע,
phrases.english: He is one who is obligated to swear and cannot swear,
and anyone who is obligated to swear
and cannot swear must pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא הָוֵה לֵיהּ מְחוּיָּב שְׁבוּעָה וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִישָּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's question from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grabber must pay because he is obligated to swear and cannot.

steps.title: רב פפא: Two agreed cases about a witness to a death
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says there is one case where everyone agrees a witness to a death is liable, and one case where everyone agrees he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees about a witness to a death that he is liable. And everyone agrees about a witness to a death that he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new pair of 'everyone agrees' cases, this time about someone who saw a husband die. He only names the two cases here, and the גמרא explains them next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Liable' and 'exempt' mean liable or exempt for falsely denying, under oath, that he knows the testimony. The same kind of witness can come out either way, depending on the details, which the גמרא is about to give.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness who testifies that someone (here, a husband) died

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד מִיתָה שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: All agree about a witness to a death that he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד מִיתָה שֶׁהוּא פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and all agree about a witness to a death that he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same 'everyone agrees' pattern as Step 2, but with a new kind of witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness to a death can be liable in one case and exempt in another, and everyone agrees on both.

steps.title: When the witness to a death is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The witness is exempt when he told only the wife, not the court. The proof is a משנה saying a woman is believed on her own word that her husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees the witness to a death is exempt when he told the wife herself and did not tell the court. As we learned: a woman who said 'My husband died' may remarry, and if she said 'My husband died,' she may do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב פפא's 'exempt' case first and backs it up with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife herself is believed to say her husband died. So once the witness has told her, she can go to the court on her own, and his later denial costs her nothing. The גמרא does not spell out this last step, but the משנה shows why it is true.

keyTerms.meaning: She may do יבום, marrying her late husband's brother

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד מִיתָה שֶׁהוּא פָּטוּר –
phrases.english: All agree about a witness to a death that he is exempt —
where he told it to her herself
and did not tell it to the court,
as we learned: A woman who said 'My husband died' may remarry,
phrases.notes: Since she is believed on her own word, his later denial does not hurt her.

phrases.english: 'My husband died' — she may do yibum.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּעֵד מִיתָה שֶׁהוּא פָּטוּר דַּאֲמַר לַהּ לְדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of רב פפא's statement from Step 10, the 'exempt' case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is exempt when he told only the wife, because she can testify for herself and loses nothing by his denial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: a woman who says 'My husband died' may remarry or do יבום on her own word.

steps.title: The case where everyone agrees the death witness is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's second case: the witness is liable when he told no one, neither the wife nor the בית דין, that the husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that a witness to a death is liable when he did not tell the wife herself and did not tell the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב פפא's statement by giving the case where everyone agrees the witness is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 he was exempt because he had already told the wife, and she is believed on her own. Here he told nobody. So his oath denying that he knows anything really cost her money: without him she cannot collect her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness who saw that someone died

steps.whatToRemember: A witness is liable only if his denial actually caused a loss. If the wife already knows from him and is believed, his denial changed nothing. If no one knows, his denial blocks her.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees regarding a witness to a death
that he is liable
in a case where he did not tell her herself
and did not tell the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכל מודים בעד מיתה שהוא חייב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's pair: Step 11 gave the exempt case, and this gives the liable case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is liable when he told neither the wife nor the בית דין, so his denial causes her to lose her כתובה.

steps.title: Does this prove witnesses about land are liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב פפא's ruling proves that witnesses made to swear about land are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we conclude from this that if someone makes witnesses swear about land, they are liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to draw a bigger rule out of רב פפא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כתובה is normally collected from the husband's land. If the witness is liable here, it seems testimony about land can make witnesses liable. That question is a known מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this / Conclude from here
Making witnesses swear about testimony concerning land

phrases.english: Conclude from this:
one who makes witnesses swear about land, they are liable?
phrases.notes: The link is that a כתובה is usually paid out of the husband's land.

steps.triggerLanguage: שמע מינה משביע עדי קרקע חייב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to draw a general rule about land from the case in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב פפא's case prove that witnesses about land are liable for a false שבועת העדות?

steps.title: No proof: maybe she grabbed movable property
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. Perhaps the case is one where the wife seized her husband's movable things as payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is a case where she seized movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 13 by suggesting a different setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wife already holds movable items of the husband's, the testimony concerns movables, not land. So רב פפא's case tells us nothing about witnesses about land, and the מחלוקת stays open.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where she seized movable property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide whether witnesses about land are liable.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the כתובה is collected from land. It could be collected from movables that she seized.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one denied and one admitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its case where one witness denied and the other admitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one denied and one admitted, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה to set up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line of the משנה is: if one witness denied and the other admitted, the one who denied is liable. The גמרא is about to ask why this needed to be said.

phrases.english: One denied and one admitted, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: the one who denied is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the death-witness topic and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one witness denied and the other admitted, the one who denied is liable.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need this case?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה already said that when both deny one after the other the first is liable, it is obvious that when one denies and the other admits, the denier is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, when both deny one after the other, you said the first is liable and the second is exempt. When one denies and one admits, do we even need to say it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה by saying its case is too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case the first denier is liable even though the second witness also denied, and the משנה rules that second witness exempt. Here the other witness was ready to testify, so the one who denied clearly caused the loss. So of course the denier is liable, and the case seems to add nothing new.

phrases.english: Now, in the case of one after the other,
where both of them deny,
you said the first is liable and the second is exempt;
where one denied and one admitted, is it necessary to say?!

steps.triggerLanguage: השתא בזה אחר זה דתרוייהו קא כפרי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה line quoted in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of 'one denied and one admitted.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר style: if the first denier is liable even when both deny, then he is surely liable when the other admits. So the case is unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is a quick retraction: תוך כדי דיבור
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means both denied, and then one quickly took back his denial and admitted within a few seconds. This teaches that a retraction within כדי דיבור counts as part of the original speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where both denied, and one of them went back and admitted within the time it takes to say a short phrase. This teaches us that anything said within that short time counts as part of the original speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה as a special case that teaches a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both witnesses first denied. But one changed his answer right away, within כדי דיבור. His admission counts as if it were his original answer. So he is treated as someone who admitted, and the one who stayed with his denial is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a special case)
Within the time it takes to say a short phrase

steps.whatToRemember: תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי: a correction made within a few seconds counts as part of what you first said.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not describing a simple case where one witness denied and the other admitted from the start. According to this answer, both denied at first, and one fixed his answer right away.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי is used all over ש״ס, in oaths, נדרים, קידושין and more.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a case where both of them denied,
and one of them went back and admitted
within the time of speaking a short phrase;
phrases.notes: This is roughly the few seconds it takes to say a short greeting.

phrases.english: and this teaches us
that within the time of speech is like speech itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 by narrowing the משנה's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא) so that it teaches a new rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes a plain case where one denied and one admitted from the start, which seems obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both denied, and one retracted within כדי דיבור. This teaches that a quick retraction counts as part of the original speech, so he counts as having admitted.

steps.title: Why would רבי יוחנן need two clauses teaching the same rule?
steps.stepSummary: For רב חסדא, the first clause teaches אפשר לצמצם and the second clause teaches תוך כדי דיבור. For רבי יוחנן, both clauses teach תוך כדי דיבור, so one of them looks extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well for רב חסדא, who explains the earlier case like רבי יוסי הגלילי. The first clause teaches that two things can happen at exactly the same moment. The second clause teaches that something said within כדי דיבור counts as part of the first statement. But for רבי יוחנן, both clauses teach תוך כדי דיבור. Why would we need the same lesson twice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares how רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן read the משנה. It challenges רבי יוחנן because his reading makes the two clauses repeat each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב חסדא explained the case of 'both denied together' like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that two events can happen at exactly the same moment. That gives the first clause its own lesson. רבי יוחנן explained it as one witness denying right after the other, within כדי דיבור. The case from step 17 also teaches כדי דיבור, so for him the משנה seems to say the same thing twice.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well for... (the opening of a 'this works, but that does not' challenge)
It is possible for two events to happen at exactly the same moment
Within the few seconds it takes to say a short greeting
The first clause / the last clause of a משנה
Why do I need two? (the same lesson seems repeated)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that the second clause teaches תוך כדי דיבור. They disagree only about what the first clause, 'both denied together,' teaches.

phrases.english: It works out well according to Rav Chisda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמוֹקֵי לַהּ לְהָהוּא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי –
phrases.english: who explains that case according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
phrases.notes: 'That case' is the משנה's case where both witnesses denied at the same time.

phrases.english: the first clause teaches that it is possible to be exactly simultaneous,
and the last clause was needed to teach us
that something said within the time of a short utterance counts as part of the speech.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
the first clause teaches 'within the time of speech,'
and the last clause also teaches 'within the time of speech'!
Why do I need two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 17, that the second clause teaches תוך כדי דיבור, and turns it into a challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה's 'both denied together' case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not teach the same rule twice. Under רבי יוחנן, both clauses teach תוך כדי דיבור, so one clause seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The second clause teaches that a denial can be taken back by an admission
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought תוך כדי דיבור joins two denials but cannot turn a denial into an admission. The second clause teaches that it can.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the rule of כדי דיבור works only for a denial followed by another denial. Maybe it would not work for a denial followed by an admission. So the משנה teaches us that it works there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and shows that even for רבי יוחנן, each clause teaches something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause shows that two denials said within כדי דיבור are treated as one statement. A person might have thought you cannot take back a denial once it is said. The second clause, where one witness denies and then admits within כדי דיבור, teaches that the admission counts and cancels his denial.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said... (introduces a mistaken assumption)
A denial (claiming not to know testimony)
It teaches us (that the mistaken assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the first clause teaches that תוך כדי דיבור joins two denials. The second teaches that it also lets a person take back a denial with an admission.

phrases.english: You might have said:
these words apply only to a denial followed by a denial,
but a denial followed by an admission, say it does not apply;
so it teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by showing that the second clause adds a new lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the second clause is needed (one might have limited the rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תוך כדי דיבור works only to join two denials, not to take back a denial with an admission.
steps.terutzMaskana: תוך כדי דיבור also works for a denial followed by an admission, so the admission counts.

steps.title: The משנה's case of two sets of witnesses denying one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה. The first set of witnesses denies, then the second set denies, and the משנה rules that both sets are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two sets of witnesses, and the first set denied knowing anything, and then the second set denied too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new case in the משנה. It quotes it to set up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case now involves two full sets of witnesses, each able to testify. The משנה rules that both sets are liable for a false שבועת העדות. The quoted words describe the case, and the גמרא is about to question it.

phrases.english: If there were two sets of witnesses,
and the first set denied knowing anything
and afterwards the second set denied too.
phrases.notes: The משנה's ruling here is that both sets are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of כדי דיבור and starts a new case from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two sets of witnesses deny one after the other, both sets are liable.

steps.title: Why is the first set of witnesses liable?
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense that the second set is liable, since after the first set denied, everything depended on them. But when the first set denied, the second set was still available, so why is the first set liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the second set is liable, because the first set had already denied. But the first set, why are they liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the first set is liable too. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses are liable for denying because their denial causes the plaintiff to lose money. Once the first set denied, the second set was his only hope, so their denial truly caused the loss. When the first set denied, the second set could still testify, so the first set's denial seems not to have caused any loss.

phrases.english: It makes sense that the second set will be liable,
since the first set had already denied;
phrases.notes: Once the first set denied, the plaintiff could only win through the second set, so their denial cost him.

phrases.english: but the first set, why are they liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling that was just quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the first set of witnesses is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses are liable only when their denial causes a loss. When the first set denied, the second set was still available to testify, so the first set's denial caused no loss.
